sections.label: Competition Act enactment purpose
sections.summary: The Competition Act was enacted in 2004 to promote efficient market conduct and strengthen Singapore's competitiveness for businesses and consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: The Competition Act was enacted in 2004 to promote efficient market conduct and to strengthen Singapore's competitiveness, for the benefit of both businesses and consumers.

sections.label: CCS accepting binding commitments
sections.summary: The first key amendment allows CCS to accept binding and enforceable commitments for cases involving sections 34 and 47 prohibitions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: The first key amendment of this Bill is to allow CCS to accept binding and enforceable commitments for cases involving sections 34 and 47 prohibitions.

sections.label: Clauses amending sections 60A 60B
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 8 amend sections 60A and 60B to let CCS accept binding commitments for sections 34 and 47 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 8 of the Bill amend sections 60A and 60B of the Competition Act, to allow CCS to similarly accept binding and enforceable commitments offered by entities for cases involving the sections 34 and 47 prohibitions.

sections.label: CCS general interviews power
sections.summary: The second key amendment empowers CCS to conduct general interviews during inspections or searches of premises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: The second key amendment is to empower CCS to conduct general interviews during such inspections or searches of premises.

sections.label: Confidential advice on anticipated mergers
sections.summary: The final key amendment allows CCS to provide confidential advice on anticipated mergers as a statutory process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: The final key amendment of this Bill is to allow CCS to provide confidential advice on anticipated mergers as a statutory process.

sections.label: Clause 4 new section 55A
sections.summary: Clause 4 introduces section 55A to formalise confidential advice on anticipated mergers, aiming to enhance the competition regime and ensure a level playing field.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: Clause 4 introduces a new section 55A to formalise CCS' provision of confidential advice on anticipated mergers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: This does not change the process by which CCS will provide their advice, but seeks to provide greater clarity and assurance to businesses which wish to consider approaching CCS for advice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: The Bill aims to enhance the efficiency and efficacy of the competition regime in Singapore and to ensure a level playing field for all businesses.

sections.label: Oral examination amendment proposal
sections.summary: The Bill proposes letting Commission officers orally examine persons on entered premises, removing the need to serve a section 63 notice, to streamline inspections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Section 63(2) of the Act further provides that such notice shall indicate the subject matter and purposes of the investigation and the nature of offences under sections 75 to 78 of the Act in the event where the person served with the section 63 notice fails to comply with the notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes to amend this position by allowing the Commission's officers to orally examine any person on the premises which they have entered pursuant to section 64 or 65 of the Act, so long as the person appears to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances relevant to the investigation being carried out and require the person to answer any question relating to the investigation, essentially doing away with the need to serve the section 63 notice on the person examined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to the Commission, the aim of the proposed amendment is not to expand the investigative powers of the Commission but to streamline the process of service of the documents during inspections and searches under section 64 and 65 of the Act to allow the Commission to conduct its inspections in a more efficient manner, thereby minimising potential disruption to the business.

sections.label: Safeguards and legal adviser questions
sections.summary: The passage asks what safeguards inform the person examined of the investigation's subject matter and purposes, and whether a legal adviser may accompany them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, with the doing away of the requirement to serve the section 63 notice on the person to be examined, what safeguards are in place to ensure that the person being examined is sufficiently informed of the subject matter and purposes of the investigation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Would a person being examined at the premises by the Commission's officers under the proposed amendment be allowed to request to be accompanied by a professional legal adviser?

sections.label: SMEs as workforce driver
sections.summary: The passage states that SMEs provide more than 60% of jobs to the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our SMEs are our key workforce driver, providing more than 60% of jobs to our local workforce.

sections.label: Revisiting Competition Act for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage suggests revisiting the Competition Act to consider local SMEs and small retail businesses in future amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, just like I have mentioned before, it would be wise, I think, if we revisit the Competition Act, to consider this aspect towards our local SMEs and small retail businesses, when making future amendments.

sections.label: Welcoming Competition Bill commitments
sections.summary: The passage welcomes the Competition Bill and amendments, and states the provisions empower the Commission to accept commitments for anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominance, besides mergers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, if otherwise, then this may result in an unhealthy market situation, which is not preferred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Competition Bill and the amendments that are being put in place are highly welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important to note that while we would like to regulate, it must not stifle the open market framework with the aim towards healthy competition for the larger benefit of the consumer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, the Competition Bill and its proposed amendments are welcomed as they are intended to ensure that the healthy competition landscape is being safeguarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These provisions empower the Commission to accept commitments for cases involving: (a) Agreements, decisions or concerted practices that may have the object or effect of preventing, restricting or distorting competition within Singapore; or (b) Conduct on the part of one or more undertakings that may amount to abuse of a dominant position in any market in Singapore, in addition to the current power to accept commitments for mergers which may result in a substantial lessening of competition within Singapore.

sections.label: Commitments under new sections
sections.summary: The passage states new sections 60A(1A) and 60A(1B) let the Commission require and accept commitments for section 34 and section 47 findings, and asks whether this eases bypassing competition law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the replacement by the new section 60A(1A) and 60A(1B), this will allow the Commission to require and accept from companies a commitment where they have been found to restrict competition under section 34 and require and accept from companies a commitment where they have been found to abuse their dominant position in a market under section 47.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here is my next question: will this make it easier for companies to bypass the competition law now that commitments may be accepted with respect to all the prohibitions of the original Act?

sections.label: Competition Bill and amendments
sections.summary: The Competition Bill and its amendments are intended to achieve the stated purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Competition Bill and its amendments are intended to do so.

sections.label: Oral examination on premises
sections.summary: New sections 63(4A) and 63(4B) allow oral examination of a person found on premises, with recorded, read-over and signed answers, without a section 63 notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 63(4A) allows a person found on the premises to be orally examined and required to produce answers relevant to the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The statement has to be recorded in writing, read over in a language understood by the examinee and signed by him under the new section 63(4B).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, as the Senior Minister of State has mentioned earlier, there is no need for such an examinee to be served with a notice under section 63 even though the examinee can now be made to answer a broader scope of questions equivalent to that under section 63.

sections.label: Commitments offered to CCS
sections.summary: Commitments offered to CCS must remedy, mitigate or prevent the adverse effects of the anti-competitive conduct under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Commitments offered to CCS must remedy, mitigate or prevent the adverse effects of the anti-competitive conduct that is currently being investigated.

sections.label: Streamlining CCS investigation process
sections.summary: The amendment seeks to streamline CCS investigations by allowing a single notice to enter premises, obtain documents, ask questions and require occupant information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The proposed amendment thus seeks to streamline CCS' investigation process, to enable CCS to serve a single notice to enter the premises to obtain documents and also ask questions pertaining to the documents found on the premises, as well as require occupants to provide information relating to the subject matter and purpose of the investigation.

sections.label: Interview with legal advisor
sections.summary: If an individual CCS wishes to examine wants his legal advisor present, CCS will allow reasonable time for the advisor to arrive at the premises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If an individual that CCS wishes to examine expresses his will to be interviewed in the presence of his legal advisor, CCS will provide a reasonable amount of time to allow the legal advisor to arrive at the premises.

sections.label: CCS decision after confidential advice
sections.summary: Mr Azmoon Ahmad asked whether CCS can still decide under section 57 after earlier providing confidential advice to the contrary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Azmoon Ahmad has asked whether CCS is still able to make a decision pursuant to section 57, which provides for the process that an anticipated merger has infringed the section 54 prohibition, after providing confidential advice to the contrary earlier.

sections.label: CCS advice not binding
sections.summary: Advice that CCS issues under the new section 55A is not binding on CCS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As such, the advice that CCS issues under the new section 55A is not binding on CCS.

sections.label: CCS further action after decision
sections.summary: CCS may take further action after a favourable merger decision if it suspects materially incomplete, false or misleading information, or a breached commitment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Notwithstanding that CCS issues a favourable decision that the anticipated merger will not infringe the section 54 prohibition, CCS may take further action if it has reasonable grounds to suspect that information on which CCS had previously based its decision was materially incomplete, false or misleading, or if a party who had provided a commitment has failed to adhere to it.
